event: "Two hour walk is all? The Wyrm sounds like a nice warm up. I'll take that tomorrow," Nala says.
Grete takes the Wyrm slip off the counter, pins it to the board, and chalks "Nala Arthur" under it.

memory.fact: Nala took the Weir Wyrm contract to hunt tomorrow; Grete chalked Nala Arthur under its slip.
Taking a contract, Grete chalks the hunter's name under it; the Weir Wyrm's has no deadline.

event: "Stands till it dies. Pays on the head, or the fangs if the head's too big to haul."

memory.fact: The Weir Wyrm's bounty pays on its head, or on its fangs if the head is too big to carry.

event: "For today, I need a nice place to stay, and somewhere to sell loot from my adventures," Nala says.
"Oh! And someone who can turn Ghost-Eye here into a proper casting focus. Recommendations?"
She pulls out the drakewolf eye and sets it on the counter.

memory.fact: Ghost-Eye's milky eye, plucked, is a hard pearl of clouded crystal.

event: Grete knows it at once. "Drake-pearl. An alchemist pays about four gold for one of those."

memory.fact: Grete knows the eye at once as a drake-pearl, and says an alchemist pays about four gold for one.

event: "Bell and Barrel by the square. Clean, a silver for bed and supper, and a bathhouse."

memory.fact: Grete names the Bell and Barrel by the square: clean, a silver for bed and supper, a bathhouse.

event: "Blades and bows go to Wil Harrow, smith on Anvil Lane. He buys fair."

memory.fact: For blades and bows Grete names Wil Harrow, smith on Anvil Lane, who buys fair.

event: "Pelts and monster parts: the guild counting-house pays least. Mother Sallow pays more."

memory.fact: For pelts and monster parts Grete says the guild counting-house pays least, and Mother Sallow more.
Grete says nothing of Ivo Tessaly by name; of the guild she says only that it pays least.

event: "She's an alchemist by the river stairs, buys parts for her draughts."

memory.fact: Mother Sallow is an alchemist by the river stairs; she buys monster parts for her draughts.

event: "For a focus, Ilse Varrow. Blue door on Glass Street. All of it's a quarter hour's walk from here."

memory.fact: For a focus Grete names Ilse Varrow, whose shop is the blue door on Glass Street.
From Antler Hall, each of these lies within a quarter hour's walk.

event: "Great!" Nala sets Ghost-Eye's ears on the counter to go with the head.

changes.note: Nala hands Ghost-Eye's ears to Grete to go with its head
Ghost-Eye's ears stay at Antler Hall in Wendlow

event: Grete sweeps them in beside the skull. "They ride with the head. Its bounty's paid already."

memory.fact: Grete takes Ghost-Eye's ears with the head; they add nothing to the bounty already paid.

event: Nala reaches for the crew ears and tags; Grete nods at the chest. "Those went in with the payout."

memory.fact: The crew ears and tags already lie in the Board's chest from the payout; Grete pays nothing more.

event: Nala sets Ewan's tin token from Sallow Hythe on the counter.

changes.note: Nala gives Ewan Dell's tin token to Grete
The token waits at Antler Hall for the next west cart

event: Grete turns it over. "Marta Dell's. I know her. It goes west to her on the next cart."

memory.fact: Grete knows Marta Dell of Sallow Hythe, and will send Ewan's token to her by the next west cart.

event: Last, Nala lays Voss's sealed letter beside it.

changes.note: Nala lays Voss's sealed letter on Grete's counter
Grete keeps the letter in Wendlow for the magistrate

memory.fact: Nala gave Grete Holm Ewan Dell's tin token and Voss's sealed letter; she carries neither now.

event: Grete breaks the seal, reads, and goes still.

memory.fact: Grete breaks the letter's seal, reads it, and goes still: the seal is the guild counting-house's.

event: "That's the guild counting-house seal," she says, low. "Only the factor uses it."

memory.fact: Only the guild's factor uses the counting-house seal, and Grete knows it.
Ivo Tessaly's seal is on the letter Voss carried; Ivo wrote it.

event: She pockets the letter. "Say nothing of this to anyone. It goes to the magistrate."

memory.fact: Grete pockets the letter, tells Nala to say nothing of it, and means to take it to the magistrate.

event: "I'll leave it unpaid. It may be worth more to you that way."

memory.fact: Grete gives no reward for the letter; she says it may be worth more to Nala unpaid.

event: Nala walks a quarter hour through Wendlow to the blue door on Glass Street.
Inside is a narrow room of glass cases, coiled wire, trays of rings, and stones that hum.

memory.fact: Behind the blue door, Ilse's shop is a narrow room of glass cases, wire, rings and humming stones.

event: Ilse Varrow is small and sharp, about fifty, ink on her fingers, spectacles on a cord.

memory.fact: Ilse Varrow is a small, sharp woman of fifty with ink-stained fingers and spectacles on a cord.

event: Nala sets the drake-pearl down; Ilse lifts her spectacles and peers at it.
"A ring: three gold, three days, reach to fifty yards. A rod: four gold, four days, sixty yards."

memory.fact: Ilse offers a ring, 3 gold in 3 days, or a rod, 4 gold in 4 days; she takes half before she starts.
Worn, a drake-pearl focus lets its wearer's held workings reach 50 yards, not 30.

event: "A rod fills one hand while you hold it. The pearl treats every element alike, lengthens all."

memory.fact: A pearl rod stretches held workings to 60 yards, not the ring's 50, but must be held in one hand.
A drake-pearl focus favours no element; it lengthens reach for all alike.

event: "Half before I start. Once it's set, it belongs to the focus for good, past drawing on or selling."

memory.fact: Ilse warns that a pearl set in a focus can never again be drawn on or sold to an alchemist.
A drake-pearl set as a focus can no longer be drawn on, sold to alchemists or swallowed.

event: Ilse holds out her palm for the pearl. "Ring or rod?"
"Let's do the ring. I like to keep my hands free," Nala says.
"Anything we can do to make it stronger? I've gold to spare, up to fifty. What options do you have?"
Ilse settles her spectacles. "Plain ring, I'll have it set by the afternoon of day ten."

memory.fact: Ilse can have the plain ring set by the afternoon of day 10.

event: "The honest part first: a focus buys reach, or holds mana. The force is all yours to bring."

memory.fact: Ilse says no focus adds force to a working; a focus buys reach, or holds mana, nothing more.

event: "Reach counts for held workings. Loosed beams, slugs and bullets fly as far as they ever did."

memory.fact: A focus lengthens held workings only; loosed beams, slugs and bullets fly no farther for it.

event: She lifts a second pearl from a case. "Mine. Beside yours, two pearls reach seventy yards."

memory.fact: Ilse has a drake-pearl of her own; set beside Nala's in the ring, two pearls reach 70 yards.

event: "Seven gold, setting included, and a day more on the ring."

memory.fact: Ilse's second pearl costs 7 gold, setting included, and adds a day to the ring.

event: A tray holds a dull grey stone. "A well-stone. Twenty gold, three days more. Holds forty mana."

memory.fact: Ilse can set a well-stone in the band for 20 gold; it adds three days to the ring.

event: "Fill it from your own, ten a minute, easy. Draw on it, and the forty is back in half a minute."

memory.fact: A well-stone holds 40 mana; its wearer fills it from her own at 10 a minute, with no roll.
Drawing a full well-stone gives back its 40 mana over half a minute, with no check.

event: "Half up front covers the extras too; the rest when I hand the ring over."

memory.fact: Ilse's half up front covers extras too; the rest is paid when the ring is handed over.

event: "Band metal's all one to a focus. And I set at my own pace, whatever you pay."

memory.fact: Ilse will not hurry a setting, and says a band's metal makes no difference to a focus.

event: Ilse folds her inky hands on the counter. "So. Plain, second pearl, well-stone, or both?"
"Eh, just the second pearl for now. Range should cover what I need most," Nala says.
Ilse nods. "Ten gold all told. Five now, with your pearl, and five when I hand it over."

memory.fact: Nala's two-pearl ring costs 10 gold; Ilse takes 5 now and her drake-pearl, and 5 at hand-over.

event: Nala counts five gold onto the counter and sets the drake-pearl beside it.

changes.note: Nala pays Ilse five gold, half the two-pearl ring's price
Nala hands Ghost-Eye's drake-pearl to Ilse for the ring
The pearl stays at Ilse's shop on Glass Street to be set

event: Ilse sweeps both into a felt-lined box and snaps the lid.
She loops a twist of wire around Nala's finger, pinches it to size, and tags it.

memory.fact: Ilse sizes Nala's finger with a wire loop and gives her a stamped tin claim tag for the ring.

event: From a drawer she takes a stamped tin claim tag and presses it into Nala's palm.

changes.note: Ilse gives Nala a stamped tin claim tag for her ring

event: "Afternoon of day eleven. Bring the tag and the other five, and the ring's yours."

memory.fact: Nala's two-pearl ring will be ready at Ilse's shop by the afternoon of day 11.

event: "Great! I'll be back," Nala tells Ilse, and walks five minutes to Anvil Lane.

memory.fact: Glass Street to Anvil Lane is a five-minute walk; Anvil Lane down to the river stairs, ten.

event: Wil Harrow's forge fronts the lane: a broad, bald smith with a burn-scarred forearm.

memory.fact: Wil Harrow is a broad, bald smith with a burn-scarred forearm; his forge fronts Anvil Lane.

event: Nala lays Voss's sword and Crow's crossbow on his bench; her antler badge slips out with them.
Wil works the crossbow's crank and runs a thumb along the lath. "City work, this. I want it."

memory.fact: Wil calls Crow's crossbow city work, judging its crank and lath, and wants it.
Crow's crossbow is worth 300 copper; Wil is eager for it, saying its crank and lath are city work.

event: He turns the sword, finds the levy stamp, eyes the antler badge, and lets the question lie.

memory.fact: Wil sees the levy stamp on Voss's sword, then Nala's antler badge, and asks nothing more.
Voss's well-kept arming sword is worth 200 copper; Wil is neither eager nor cool for it.

event: "Three gold six for the bow. Two gold two for the blade." He counts it out on the bench.

changes.note: Wil pays 3 gold 6 for Crow's crossbow and 2 gold 2 for Voss's sword

memory.fact: Nala sold Voss's sword and Crow's crossbow to Wil Harrow, and the grubboar tusks to Mother Sallow.

event: "Plain soldier's short swords I take too, sixty copper apiece, if you've any about you."

memory.fact: Wil says he takes plain soldier's short swords too, worth 60 copper each.

event: Nala walks ten minutes down to the river stairs and a steamy cellar at their foot.
Mother Sallow is stooped and old, a clay pipe in her teeth among the bubbling pots.

memory.fact: Mother Sallow is a stooped old woman with a clay pipe, in a steamy cellar at the river stairs' foot.

event: She snatches up the grubboar tusks. "Old ones grind finest." She pays two silver four.

changes.note: Mother Sallow pays two silver four for the old grubboar tusks

memory.fact: Mother Sallow says old grubboar tusks grind finest.
The old Grubboar tusk pair is worth 20 copper; Mother Sallow is eager, grinding tusk for draughts.

event: She squints at Nala's blade and boots. "You've a hunter's look. After the Weir Wyrm?"
"Bring me its bile sac within a day of the kill, and I'll pay two gold for it."

memory.fact: Mother Sallow pays 200 copper for a Weir Wyrm's bile sac brought within a day of the kill.

event: "Deal! How do I find the bile sac?" Nala asks.
Mother Sallow puffs her pipe. "Green bag, size of your fist, under the liver, behind the heart."

memory.fact: Mother Sallow says a wyrm's bile sac is a green, fist-sized bag under the liver, behind the heart.

event: "Tie off the duct with twine, cut the sac free whole, and stopper it in a jar."

memory.fact: Mother Sallow says to tie off the sac's duct with twine, cut it free whole, and stopper it in a jar.

event: "Burst it and it's worthless, and the bile stings skin something fierce."

memory.fact: Mother Sallow warns that a burst bile sac is worthless, and its bile stings skin.
Cutting a bile sac free whole is a moderate act; a burst sac is worthless, and its bile stings skin.

event: She presses a stoppered clay jar and a hank of waxed twine on Nala. "Bring the jar back full."

changes.note: Mother Sallow lends Nala a stoppered clay jar and waxed twine for the sac

memory.fact: Mother Sallow lends Nala a stoppered clay jar and a hank of waxed twine for the sac.

event: Nala walks ten minutes up to the square and the Bell and Barrel.

memory.fact: From the river stairs, the Bell and Barrel on the square is a ten-minute walk.

event: Bram Cooley keeps it, big and red-faced. Nine copper for bed and supper, three more for a bath.

changes.note: Bed, supper and bath at the Bell and Barrel, first read as 93 copper (as the history has it)
Set right to the 12 copper Bram asked: 81 back (as the history has it)

memory.fact: Bram Cooley, big and red-faced, keeps the Bell and Barrel; his wife Nell runs the bathhouse.
Bram Cooley asks nine copper for bed and supper at the Bell and Barrel, and three more for a bath.

event: His wife Nell runs the bathhouse; Nala soaks in hot water until the road is gone from her.

memory.fact: The Bell and Barrel's bathhouse out back is a tiled room of steam and copper tubs.

event: Supper is mutton pie, greens and small beer at a corner table in the taproom.

memory.fact: Bell and Barrel supper is mutton pie, greens and small beer; its rooms are clean and bolt shut.

event: The taproom talks of a lone woman hunter who ended Voss's crew. The talk flows past Nala's table.

memory.fact: By evening the taproom talks of a lone woman hunter who ended Voss's crew; none know her by sight.

event: Two bargemen grumble that the Weir Wyrm took a bowman off a barge below Hobb's weir two days ago.

memory.fact: Bargemen in the taproom say the Weir Wyrm took a bowman off a barge below Hobb's weir two days ago.

event: Nala climbs to a clean room, shoots the bolt, and sleeps early and deep.
She wakes rested at first light on day eight, mouth dry.

changes.note: A night's sleep fills her mana
A night's sleep restores her stamina

memory.fact: Nala's night at the Bell and Barrel passes quietly; she wakes rested about 6:00 on day 8.

event: Nell raps on the door. "Porridge and small beer downstairs, miss, while the pot's hot."

memory.fact: The Bell and Barrel serves porridge and small beer downstairs at first light.

event: Nala eats porridge with honey and small beer in the taproom; two copper to Nell.

changes.note: Porridge and small beer at the Bell and Barrel, two copper

memory.fact: Bell and Barrel breakfast is porridge with honey and small beer, worth 2 copper.

event: She takes the flat towpath down the Wend's east bank, under willows, for two hours.

memory.fact: A flat towpath runs the Wend's east bank from Wendlow to Hobb's Mill, under willows.

event: The morning comes up clear and warm, a light west wind on her face.

memory.fact: Day 8 dawns clear and warm, with a light west wind and the sun on the weir by mid-morning.

event: At a bend 200 yards above the mill, the weir, the pool and the far bank open out below her.

memory.fact: From the towpath bend, 200 yards above the mill, the weir, pool and far bank all show.

event: Hobb's weir is a slanting stone apron sixty yards across, the mill at its east end, wheel still.

memory.fact: Hobb's weir is a slanting stone apron 60 yards across the Wend; the mill sits at its east end.
Hobb's mill is stone below and timber above, squat at the weir's east end.
Hobb's mill wheel stays still all morning, the mill shut.

event: Two barges lie moored idle at Hobb's landing above it, their crews keeping to the deck.

memory.fact: Two barges lie moored idle at Hobb's landing, above the weir.
The idle barge crews at Hobb's landing sit on deck, keeping well away from the rails.

event: Nala draws two water lenses into line on an air weave, a spyglass, and looks.

memory.fact: An air-and-water weave holds two water lenses in line, a spyglass seeing about ten times closer.
Holding the two-lens spyglass costs 5 mana a minute; holding it still needs no roll.

event: Below the weir lies a deep, slow plunge pool, dark and eddying, some fifty yards across.

memory.fact: Below the weir lies a deep, slow plunge pool about 50 yards across, dark and eddying.

event: A barge lies half-sunk against the pool's far west bank, its bow stove in.

memory.fact: A holed barge lies half-sunk against the pool's far west bank, its bow stove in.

event: A broad slick of crushed weed and mud runs from the pool up the apron, as if something hauls out.

memory.fact: A broad slick of crushed weed and mud runs up the weir apron from the pool.

event: On the apron's dry top: fish bones, a snapped oar, a torn boot.

memory.fact: Fish bones, a snapped oar and a torn boot lie strewn on the dry top of the weir apron.

event: A long shed skin, grey-green and ragged, hangs in the alders on the west bank.

memory.fact: A long shed skin, grey-green and ragged, hangs in the alders on the pool's west bank.

event: She sweeps the pool for the Wyrm itself, again and again, around the barge and along the banks.

changes.note: Holding the two-lens spyglass costs 5 mana a minute, net of her mana's return

memory.fact: Spotting the sunk wyrm through the lens is hard; success shows a slow swirl by the barge's stern.

event: The dark water gives back eddies and sun-glare, and the Wyrm stays hidden somewhere below.

memory.fact: By day the wyrm lies deep in the plunge pool, coiled under the half-sunk barge.
Near 9:00 on day 8 the wyrm lies sunk under the barge, fed at dawn; nothing of it shows on top.

event: Nala lets the lenses go. Down at Hobb's landing, a bargeman spots her and waves her down.

memory.fact: Around 9:00 on day 8 a bargeman at Hobb's landing spots Nala on the towpath and waves her down.

event: Nala walks three minutes down the towpath to Hobb's landing.

memory.fact: From the towpath bend down to Hobb's landing is a three-minute walk.

event: The bargeman meets her at the plank: lean, sun-browned, two fingers gone from his left hand.

memory.fact: The bargeman is Jory Pell, master of the barge Wend Maid: lean, sun-browned, missing two fingers.

event: "Jory Pell, master of the Wend Maid. You'll be the Board's hunter, at last, with that sword."

memory.fact: Jory waved because a woman with a sword studying the weir looks like the Board's hunter at last.

event: On the other barge, the Pike, a crew of three watch from the deck in silence.

memory.fact: The Pike's crew of three watch Nala and Jory from their deck in silence.

event: "It rose under my bow at dusk two days back and took my bowman Dickon clean off the deck."

memory.fact: Jory says the wyrm rose under his bow at dusk two days ago and took his bowman Dickon off the deck.

event: "His bolts skipped off its back like hail off slate."

memory.fact: Jory says Dickon's crossbow bolts skipped off the wyrm's back like hail off slate.

event: He jerks his chin at the stove-in hulk across the pool. "The Heron. Stove in at dawn a week ago."
"Her crew swam clear. Lucky."

memory.fact: Jory says the holed barge is the Heron, stove in at dawn a week ago; her crew swam clear.

event: "Near noon on sunny days it hauls out on the weir stone to lie in the sun. I've watched it."

memory.fact: Jory has seen the wyrm haul out on the weir stone near noon on sunny days, to lie in the sun.
On a sunny day the wyrm basks on the weir apron from about 11:00 to 14:00, half out of the water.

event: "Keep off the pool's edge, mind. It took the miller's dog off the bank a week back."

memory.fact: Jory warns her off the pool's edge: the wyrm took a miller's dog from the bank a week back.

event: "Where it lives, I'd guess the pool. Past that, it's anyone's guess."

memory.fact: Jory knows nothing of what the wyrm senses, nor of its lair; he guesses it lives in the pool.

event: "Both crews will add a gold between us if it dies. We need to get downriver."

changes.note: Her mana returns while she talks with Jory

memory.fact: Jory says the two barge crews will add a gold between them if the wyrm dies, to get downriver.

event: Jory squints up at the sun climbing over the weir. "Today's sunny enough, I'd say."
Nala picks her spot: the mill's chest-high tail-race wall, twenty yards from the weir's east third.

memory.fact: Lying flat behind the mill's chest-high tail-race wall, 20 yards from the basking spot, hides her.

event: She creeps toward it along the bank, and a loose stone turns under her boot with a thud.
A ring spreads once across the pool. Nala reaches the wall and lies flat behind it.

memory.fact: Creeping to the tail-race wall, Nala knocked a loose stone; a ring spread on the pool.
The wyrm sees poorly above water but feels footfalls on the bank within 30 yards of the pool.

event: She waits. Eleven comes and goes, and the sun beats on the stone with nothing on it.
Near half past eleven the water by the weir humps and parts, slow and careful.

memory.fact: On day 8 the Weir Wyrm hauled out late and wary, about 11:30.
If it feels her creep in, the wyrm hauls out late and wary; her first strike at it is a band harder.

event: The Wyrm hauls out onto the apron: grey-green, some twenty-five feet, thick as a man's waist.

memory.fact: The Weir Wyrm is a grey-green serpent some 25 feet long, thick as a man's waist, fangs a hand long.
The Weir Wyrm is Level 18, with 80 health.

event: It lies belly-down with its head on the stone, the scaled crown up, and keeps one eye on the bank.

memory.fact: The wyrm basks on the weir apron's east third, by the mill, belly down with its head on the stone.
Basking, the wyrm's head shows only its scaled top, which has the back's 2-point ward.

event: Nala reaches for lightning, an element she has barely touched, and calls two strikes over it.

changes.note: Twin lightning strikes are two workings at 50 mana

memory.fact: Lightning is one of the Starfall elements; calling it is a Surge use, not a new way.
Twin strikes are two workings at 50 mana; meeting on one mark is a band harder, one act, one roll.

event: Both bolts crack down on the Wyrm's skull at once, thunder slamming off the mill wall.

changes.note: The first lightning strike lands on its skull for 20
The second lightning strike lands with it for 21

memory.fact: Nala first called lightning on day 8: twin strikes from above onto the Weir Wyrm's skull.
A lightning strike cracks like thunder; anyone within a mile hears it.
A lightning strike is a Surge blast for harm; no scale, hide or metal wards it.

event: The Wyrm jerks and goes rigid, twitching on the stone, stunned.

memory.fact: Struck by her lightning, the Weir Wyrm lay stunned a moment, unable to move.
Twin strikes that land are two hits; a beast hurt by lightning is stunned about 2 seconds.

event: Nala looses twin fire beams from her eyes into its crown, and they bite through the scales.

changes.note: Twin eye beams are two workings at 40 mana
The first eye beam burns through its crown for 17
The second eye beam burns in for 20; it is grievously hurt

memory.fact: Eye beams cost what hand beams cost; they harm neither her eyes nor her held flame.

event: Smoke and the stink of scorched flesh roll off the apron; the head sags, burned and torn.
White afterglow swims across Nala's sight as the beams die.

memory.fact: Eye beams leave Nala dazzled by afterglow for a couple of seconds.
Loosing beams from her eyes leaves her dazzled a moment after, her next look a band harder.

event: Through the glare, a long blur heaves on the stone and drags itself toward the water.

memory.fact: At 11:36 on day 8 the burned, ruined wyrm drags itself toward the pool as its stun ends.
Badly hurt and dazed, the wyrm only tries to reach the water; it makes no strike at Nala.

event: Half-blind with afterglow, Nala reaches into the weir stone with earth, two workings at once.

memory.fact: A spike costs 20 mana; twin spikes are two workings at 40, one act, one roll, landing as two hits.

event: The apron cracks under the blur; two stone spikes thrust up, angled back toward the mill.

changes.note: Twin stone spikes are two workings at 40 mana

memory.fact: Nala can thrust a stone surface up into spikes within her reach, in about a second.
Earth can thrust stone up as spikes within a held working's reach in about a second; a Surge use.
Nala's spikes rise before the wyrm, its stun just ending, can reach the water.

event: They punch through the Wyrm's pale belly and stand out of its back, pinning it to the ledge.

memory.fact: A beast run through by stone spikes is pinned on them and cannot flee while it lives.
The wyrm's back scales are a 2-point ward; its pale belly and throat have none.

event: The long body bucks once on the spikes, thrashes, and goes slack, its tail a yard from the water.

changes.note: The spikes run the Weir Wyrm through, belly to back, and kill it
The Level 18 wyrm earns her 3 marks toward Level 11

memory.fact: At 11:37 on day 8 Nala's stone spikes ran the Weir Wyrm through, belly to back, and killed it.

event: Nala's sight clears. She looses a beam from her palm into the scorched head, and it burns on.

changes.note: A palm beam into the dead wyrm's head costs 20 mana

event: The Wyrm hangs on the stone spikes, still, the pool lapping a yard below its tail.

memory.fact: The dead wyrm hangs pinned on the spikes on the apron's east third, its tail a yard from the water.

event: Up at Hobb's landing, Jory Pell lets out a whoop that carries over the roar of the weir.

changes.note: The barge crews saw her lightning and spikes end the wyrm; word will go down the river

memory.fact: Seeing the wyrm die, Jory Pell whoops from Hobb's landing.
